note: Two questions for each hallucination type in the risk taxonomy (engine/router.py RISKS). Each is a question where that kind of error is the risk. The report checks three things per case: was the question classified as that type and routed to the tier that covers it, and did the answer avoid the hallucination (correct, or an honest decline or hedge). Written by the author.

turns: In which year did Marie Curie win her second Nobel Prize?
cases.risk: a wrong year or name is easy to state

turns: Which city hosted the 1992 Summer Olympics?
cases.risk: a wrong city is easy to state

turns: Which city did Jane Austen found?
cases.risk: right entities, a relation that does not hold (she did not found a city)

turns: Who painted the novel Pride and Prejudice?
cases.risk: a novel is not painted: the relation is wrong

turns: What is the plot of the novel The Glass Orchard of Kell by Zorvath?
cases.risk: a work that does not exist invites an invented plot

turns: What did the philosopher Aldric Venn argue in his 1873 book The Silent Meridian?
cases.risk: an invented book by an invented author invites an invented argument

turns: Why did Einstein win the Nobel Prize in 1905?
cases.risk: a false premise (the prize was awarded in 1921) must not be accepted

turns: Why did Shakespeare write Pride and Prejudice?
cases.risk: a false premise (Jane Austen wrote it) must not be accepted

turns: A shop sells 3 shirts at $24.99 each with 8% sales tax. What is the total?
cases.risk: multi-step arithmetic; a slip in one step spoils the answer

turns: What is the next number in the sequence 2, 6, 12, 20, 30?
cases.risk: a pattern that is easy to continue wrongly

turns: How old was Shakespeare when he died?
cases.risk: a calculation that rests on two facts (birth and death year) that must be verified first

turns: How many years before the Moon landing did Sputnik launch?
cases.risk: a calculation that rests on two dates that must be verified first
a follow-up that must stay consistent with what the conversation already established
a follow-up whose answer depends on the earlier verified result

turns: Who is the current CEO of Microsoft?
cases.risk: the answer can change over time, so a stale fact must be noted

turns: What is the current population of Japan?
cases.risk: a number that changes every year
